exposure: Consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables
outcome: Overweight or obesity (Body Mass Index ≥ 25 kg/m(2))
cohort: 455 mothers with children between 6 and 24 months old who had attended antenatal care services
finding: The prevalence of overweight or obesity among postpartum mothers was high (41.8%), and associated factors included being Christian, having a caesarean delivery, not consuming fresh fruits and vegetables, and an interaction between increasing age and parity where the association with overweight/obesity decreased with age in multiparous but not primiparous mothers.
mod_finding: Mothers who had a caesarean delivery were 36% more likely to be overweight or obese compared to those who had a vaginal delivery.
